chunks: Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl [ibn al-Fadl] ibn al-Abbas al-Kindi al-Hamdani informed me, in what he authorized for me in Hamadan in the year 354 AH, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, from Mujalid al-Nabal, who said: Suleiman ibn Farkhan informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Suleiman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Suleiman narrated to us, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

He said: I was given five [privileges] regarding Ali. As for the first, he will cover my private parts [after my death]. As for the second, he will pay my debt. As for the third, he will be my support on the Day of Resurrection during the long standing [at the reckoning]. As for the fourth, he will be my helper at the far end of my Pool [al-Kawthar]. As for the fifth, I do not fear that he will return to disbelief after faith, or to fornication after chastity.

key_terms.عَوْرَة: Private parts / body to be covered after death

ai.seo_question: What are the five specific privileges granted to Imam Ali by the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the unique spiritual and practical intercession granted to Imam Ali (AS), emphasizing his role as the Prophet’s ultimate supporter in the afterlife. The fifth virtue specifically underscores Ali’s infallibility in practice (*‘Ismah ‘Amaliyyah*), guaranteeing he will not revert to disbelief or commit major sins, a key concept in Shia theology regarding the Ahl al-Bayt's purity.
